analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, a developer testing guide. Three edits: the 'Last updated' date (line 3), the CI runner description for the cluster runtime tests (about line 1243, now pointing to build.md#ci-runner-routing), and the runner-routing test description (about lines 1807-1811, which now says release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners and routed jobs have per-shard lanes). The supplied units (base lines 1-927) cover only the first part of the file; the hunks at 1243 and 1807 sit outside the visible text. I could examine them only through the patch excerpt, so I cite no lines there.

I found no runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache behavior or wire protocol changes. The threat model assets (A-001 to A-019) and boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012) are not touched. The retained prefix-cache text (T-041) is test documentation only; it introduces no new storage, TTL or gating behavior.

There is one small residual concern. The doc change reports that CI macOS jobs move from literal Blacksmith runners to a routed 'plane' for the runner-routing checks. The release-workflow pinning to literal Blacksmith runners is preserved. Whether the actual CI and workflow changes make release or signing jobs run on untrusted runners is outside the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract for any reviewer of the workflow files. This documentation edit alone does not create a regression.
